source_text:
ἵνα δὲ μὴ τὴν ἐντολὴν ἢ τὸν ταύτην δεδωκότα θεὸν αἰτιάσωνταί τινες, γείτονι καὶ ὁμοσπόρῳ ἐχρήσατο ῥήματι τοιάδε φάσκων· οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι ὁ νόμος ἅγιος καὶ ἡ ἐντολὴ ἁγία καὶ δικαία καὶ
ἀγαθή. Ἐπεὶ οὖν οὐδ' αὐτὴ ἡ ἁμαρτία, τοῦτ' ἔστιν ὁ διάβολος, φύσει καὶ οὐσίᾳ ἁμαρτία ἐστίν, ἐπιφέρει λέγων· ἵνα γένηται καθ' ὑπερ 4 βολὴν ἁμαρτωλὸς ἡ ἁμαρτία διὰ τῆς ἐντολῆς. τὸ γὰρ κατ' οὐσίαν τὶ ὂν τὸ πλέον καὶ τὸ ἔλαττον οὐκ ἐπιδέξεται· ἔστιν γὰρ ὅπερ ἐστίν, ἀεὶ τοῦτο ὂν ὅπερ ἐστὶν οὐσιωδῶς. τῷ γὰρ γινομένῳ καὶ ἐπιγινομένῳ τι, εἴτε ὀλίγον εἴτε καθ' ὑπερβολήν, ἕτερός ἐστι κατ' οὐσίαν τῶν αὐτῷ ἐπιγινομένων· τὸ γὰρ πόσον οὐκ οὐσία ἀλλὰ περὶ τὴν οὐσίαν ἐστίν, οὐκ ὂν οὐσία. ἡ ἄρα τοίνυν καλουμένη ὑπὸ τοῦ ἀποστόλου ἁμαρτία τὸ πλέον ἐπιδεχομένη ἁμαρτήσειν, ἵνα γένηται καθ' ὑπερβολὴν ἁμαρτωλὸς ἡ ἁμαρτία. ἄρα καὶ τοῦ εἶναι ἁμαρτία, ᾗ ἁμαρτία ἐστίν, ἀρχὴν ἔλαβεν, οὐκ οὖσα καθ' ὑπερβολὴν ἐν ἀρχῇ κατὰ τὸ ἡμαρτηκέναι ἁμαρτωλὸς ἡ ἁμαρτία. διὸ δὴ καὶ τὴν ἐπίτασιν τοῦ γενέσθαι καθ' ὑπερβολὴν ἁμαρτωλὸν ἐσομένῳ χρόνῳ σημαίνει οὕτω λέγων· ἵνα γένηται καθ' ὑπερβολὴν ἁμαρτωλὸς ἡ ἁμαρτία διὰ τῆς ἐντολῆς. εἰ δὲ λέγοιεν· καὶ πῶς ἂν εἴη ἀγαθὴ καὶ δικαία; πῶς δὲ ἁγία ἡ ἐντολὴ καὶ ὁ νόμος, ὁπότε διὰ τῆς ἀφορμῆς αὐτῶν 2 ἁμαρτωλὸς καθ' ὑπερβολὴν ἐγένετο ἁμαρτωλὸς ἡ ἁμαρτία; πρὸς ταῦτα ἀκουέτωσαν ὅτι οὐκ, εἴ τι καταβλάπτεται, ἤδη καὶ ἡ ἀφορμὴ δι' ἣν βλάπτεται φαύλη ἐστὶ καὶ πονηρά· οὐδὲ γὰρ ὅτι οἱ ἀνόδως καὶ ἀμέτρως ἐνατενίζοντες τῷ ἡλίῳ βλάπτονται τὰς ὄψεις, ἤδη καὶ τὸν ἥλιόν φαμεν πονηρόν· οὐδ' ὅτι καθ' ὑπερβολὴν ὁ διάβολος ἁμαρτωλὸς γέγονε τῷ ἐπικεχειρηκέναι κατὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ, ἤδη καὶ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ φαῦλον καὶ πονηρὸν εἶναι λέγομεν. Οἶδα δὲ ὅτι οὐκ οἰκεῖ ἐν ἐμοί, τοῦτ' ἔστιν ἐν τῇ σαρκί μου, ἀγαθόν. νῦν εἰς τὸ τοῦ Ἀδὰμ πρόσωπον ἐξηγεῖται. καὶ ὅτι στερηθεὶς τὸν θεὸν ἔχειν ἐν ἑαυτῷ, ἀντὶ τῆς ὄντως ζωῆς θάνατον καταλλαξάμενος–καὶ γὰρ θάνατος οὐχ ὁ κοινὸς μόνος τῶν μελῶν αὐτοῦ ἐκράτησεν, ἀλλὰ καὶ ὁ τῆς παρακοῆς κατὰ τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτοῦ εἰσβαλών· μάλιστα γὰρ ὁ κρατῶν θάνατος πρὸ τῆς τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐπιδημίας ἐβασίλευσε, κατὰ πάντων νόμον καὶ σκῆπτρον τῆς ἑαυτοῦ βασιλείας ἔχων τὴν παρακοήν. ἀλλ' οὐκ ἄναρχος ἢ ἀγέννητος ἡ τοῦ θανάτου βασιλεία· ἐκ γὰρ τῶν ζώντων τὸ τεθνάναι συμβαίνει, καὶ ἐκ τῆς τῶν ὑπηκόων ὑπακοῆς τὸ παρακοῦσαί τινα. τὸ γὰρ θέλειν παράκειταί μοι, τὸ δὲ κατεργάζεσθαι τὸ καλὸν οὔ· ὃ γὰρ θέλω ἀγαθὸν τοῦτο οὐ ποιῶ, ἀλλ' ὃ μισῶ τοῦτο πράσσω. εἰ τὸ θέλειν μόνον ἐν ἡμῖν ἔστιν, τὸ δὲ κατεργάζεσθαι τὸ θεληθὲν καλὸν οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν ἡμῖν, εἰς μάτην ὁ ἀγαθὸς θεὸς τὰς ὁμοουσίας ἑαυτοῦ ψυχὰς ἐν τοῖς σώμασι κατέπεμψεν· τὸ γὰρ αὐτῷ καὶ αὐταῖς φίλον οὐ πράττουσιν, οὐκ ἐνεργοῦσιν, ἀλλὰ μόνον θέλουσιν· τάχα δὲ οὐδ' αὐτό, ἄδηλον γάρ.
thought_title: The commandment is holy; sin is not sin by nature but became sin beyond measure
orientation: Didymus is explaining Paul's words in Romans 7, arguing that the commandment and law are holy, just, and good, while 'sin' means the devil, who is not sin by nature but became sin beyond measure through the commandment.
pass_a_gloss: But so that some may not blame the commandment or the God who gave it, he used a neighboring and kindred word, saying such things: 'But we know that the law is holy and the commandment is holy and just and good.' Since therefore not even sin itself, that is, the devil, is sin by nature and substance, he adds, saying: 'So that sin might become sinful beyond measure through the commandment.' For what is something according to substance will not admit the more and the less; for it is what it is, always being what it is substantially. For what comes to be and what accrues to something, whether little or beyond measure, is other in substance than the things accruing to it; for quantity is not substance but is around the substance, not being substance. Therefore then the thing called sin by the apostle, admitting the more of sinning, so that sin might become sinful beyond measure. Therefore also of being sin, as it is sin, it took a beginning, sin not being in the beginning beyond measure according to having sinned, sinful sin. Therefore indeed he signifies the intensification of becoming beyond measure sinful in time to come, saying thus: 'So that sin might become sinful beyond measure through the commandment.' But if they should say: 'And how would the commandment and the law be good and just? And how holy, when through the occasion of them sin became sinful beyond measure, sinful sin?' To these things let them hear that not, if something is harmed, is already also the occasion through which it is harmed base and evil; for neither because those who gaze at the sun without limit and without measure are harmed in their eyes, do we already say that the sun is evil; nor because the devil has become sinful beyond measure by having attacked the son of God, do we already say that the son of God is base and evil. 'But I know that good does not dwell in me, that is, in my flesh.' Now he explains into the person of Adam. And that having been deprived of having God in himself, having exchanged death for the life that truly is—for not only the common death of his members mastered him, but also the death of disobedience entered against his soul; for especially the mastering death reigned before the coming of Christ, having disobedience as law and scepter of his own kingdom against all. But the kingdom of death is not without beginning or unbegotten; for dying happens from the living, and someone's disobeying from the obedience of the obedient. 'For the willing lies beside me, but the working out of the good is not; for the good that I will, this I do not do, but what I hate, this I practice.' If the willing alone is in us, but the working out of the willed good is not in us, in vain did the good God send down the souls of the same substance as himself into bodies; for they do not practice, they do not effect, what is dear to him and to them, but only will it; perhaps not even this, for it is unclear.

choices.english: he used a neighboring and kindred word
choices.why: Literal rendering of the metaphor: Paul used a word close in sense and related in kind to the commandment, i.e., 'law,' to avoid blaming the commandment or God.
The glossary sense of 'sin' as the devil requires keeping the adjective 'sinful' literal; 'beyond measure' renders the intensification Didymus is analyzing.

choices.term: τὸ πλέον καὶ τὸ ἔλαττον οὐκ ἐπιδέξεται
choices.english: will not admit the more and the less
choices.why: Literal philosophical language about substance and quantity; 'admit' preserves the technical sense of receiving degrees.
rejected: does not allow increase or decrease

choices.why: Literal rendering of the Aristotelian distinction between substance and accidents; 'around' preserves the spatial metaphor of quantity as non-essential.

choices.term: νῦν εἰς τὸ τοῦ Ἀδὰμ πρόσωπον ἐξηγεῖται
choices.english: Now he explains into the person of Adam
choices.why: The brief specifies this exact phrase as marking the shift to Adam's persona; 'into the person' is literal and preserves the direction of the explanation.
rejected: now he interprets it as Adam speaking
now he expounds it in Adam's character

choices.term: νόμον καὶ σκῆπτρον τῆς ἑαυτοῦ βασιλείας ἔχων τὴν παρακοήν
choices.english: having disobedience as law and scepter of his own kingdom
choices.why: Literal rendering of the metaphor: disobedience is both the law and the royal scepter of death's kingdom; 'scepter' preserves the regal image.
rejected: having disobedience as the rule and authority of his kingdom
holding disobedience as law and rod of his reign

pass_b_english: So that no one would blame the commandment or the God who gave it, he used a neighboring and kindred word, saying: “We know that the law is holy, and the commandment is holy and just and good” (Romans 7:12). Since sin itself—that is, the devil—is not sin by nature and substance, he adds: “So that sin might become sinful beyond measure through the commandment” (Romans 7:13). For what is something by substance will not admit the more and the less; it is what it is, always being what it is essentially. For what comes to be and accrues something to it, whether little or beyond measure, is other in substance than the things accruing to it. Quantity is not substance but is around the substance, not being substance. Therefore the one called sin by the apostle, admitting more sinning, so that sin might become sinful beyond measure—then it also received a beginning of being sin, insofar as it is sin, not being sinful beyond measure in the beginning, in accordance with its having sinned. Therefore he indicates the intensification of becoming sinful beyond measure in time to come, saying: “So that sin might become sinful beyond measure through the commandment” (Romans 7:13). But if they say: How could the commandment and the law be good and just? How could they be holy, when through their occasion sin became sinful beyond measure? Let them hear in response that if something is harmed, the occasion through which it is harmed is not therefore already base and evil. For it is not because those who gaze at the sun improperly and without measure harm their eyes that we say the sun is evil; nor is it because the devil became sinful beyond measure by plotting against the Son of God that we say the Son of God is base and evil. “I know that good does not dwell in me, that is, in my flesh” (Romans 7:18). Now he explains into the person of Adam. And because he was deprived of having God in himself, having exchanged true life for death—for not only the common death of his members took hold of him, but also the death of disobedience having invaded his soul. For the ruling death reigned especially before the coming of Christ, reigned over all, having disobedience as law and scepter of his own kingdom. But the kingdom of death is not without beginning or unbegotten; for dying comes from the living, and the disobedience of someone arises from the obedience of those who obey. “For willing lies close to me, but working out the good does not. For the good I will, I do not do, but the evil I hate, this I practice” (Romans 7:18-19). If willing alone is in us, but working out the willed good is not in us, then the good God sent souls of the same substance as himself into bodies in vain; for they do not do what is dear to him and to them, they do not enact it, but only will it—and perhaps not even that, for it is unclear.

problems.quote: the death of disobedience entered against his soul
problems.source_quote: ὁ τῆς παρακοῆς κατὰ τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτοῦ εἰσβαλών
problems.why: εἰσβαλών is aorist participle 'having invaded/attacked,' not 'entered against'; violent intrusion lost.
problems.fix: the death of disobedience having invaded his soul

problems.quote: having exchanged death for true life
problems.source_quote: ἀντὶ τῆς ὄντως ζωῆς θάνατον καταλλαξάμενος
problems.why: Wrong direction: Adam exchanged death FOR true life (i.e., got death instead of life), not 'death for true life.'
problems.fix: having exchanged true life for death
problems.ruling: ἀντί + gen. = 'instead of'; Adam got death instead of true life, not 'exchanged death for life.'

edits.old: having exchanged death for true life
edits.new: having exchanged true life for death

edits.old: the death of disobedience entered against his soul
edits.new: the death of disobedience having invaded his soul

fixed: Corrected: 'having exchanged death for true life' misstates the direction of the exchange; source ἀντὶ τῆς ὄντως ζωῆς θάνατον καταλλαξάμενος means he got death instead of true life.
Corrected: 'entered against his soul' loses the violent force of εἰσβαλών ('having invaded'); changed to 'having invaded his soul'.

problems.quote: not being sinful beyond measure in the beginning according to its having sinned
problems.source_quote: οὐκ οὖσα καθ' ὑπερβολὴν ἐν ἀρχῇ κατὰ τὸ ἡμαρτηκέναι ἁμαρτωλὸς ἡ ἁμαρτία
problems.why: Word order distorted; 'according to its having sinned' modifies 'sinful,' not 'in the beginning.'
problems.fix: not being sinful beyond measure in the beginning, in accordance with its having sinned

problems.quote: For dying comes from the living
problems.source_quote: ἐκ γὰρ τῶν ζώντων τὸ τεθνάναι συμβαίνει
problems.why: τὸ τεθνάναι is 'death' as event/result, not 'dying' as process; and 'comes from' weakens συμβαίνει ('comes about').
problems.fix: For death comes about from the living

edits.old: not being sinful beyond measure in the beginning according to its having sinned
edits.new: not being sinful beyond measure in the beginning, in accordance with its having sinned

edits.old: For dying comes from the living
edits.new: For death comes about from the living

fixed: Fixed 'according to its having sinned' to 'in accordance with its having sinned' with comma, since κατὰ τὸ ἡμαρτηκέναι modifies ἁμαρτωλὸς, not ἐν ἀρχῇ.
Fixed 'dying comes from' to 'death comes about from', since τὸ τεθνάναι is the event of death and συμβαίνει means 'comes about'.

problems.quote: having disobedience as law and scepter of his own kingdom over all
problems.source_quote: κατὰ πάντων νόμον καὶ σκῆπτρον τῆς ἑαυτοῦ βασιλείας ἔχων τὴν παρακοήν
problems.why: κατὰ πάντων goes with ἐβασίλευσε: 'reigned over all,' not modifying 'kingdom'; misattributed.
problems.fix: reigned over all, having disobedience as law and scepter of his own kingdom

problems.quote: someone's disobedience comes from the obedience of those who obey
problems.source_quote: ἐκ τῆς τῶν ὑπηκόων ὑπακοῆς τὸ παρακοῦσαί τινα
problems.why: τὸ παρακοῦσαί τινα is articular infinitive: 'the disobedience of someone,' not 'someone's disobedience comes from.'
problems.fix: the disobedience of someone arises from the obedience of those who obey

edits.old: having disobedience as law and scepter of his own kingdom over all
edits.new: reigned over all, having disobedience as law and scepter of his own kingdom

edits.old: someone's disobedience comes from the obedience of those who obey
edits.new: the disobedience of someone arises from the obedience of those who obey

fixed: κατὰ πάντων goes with ἐβασίλευσε: 'reigned over all,' not modifying 'kingdom'; fixed.
τὸ παρακοῦσαί τινα is articular infinitive: 'the disobedience of someone,' not 'someone's disobedience comes from'; fixed.

dismissed.quote: having disobedience as law and scepter of his own kingdom
dismissed.why: κατὰ πάντων goes with ἐβασίλευσε, not with 'having'; 'reigned over all, having disobedience as law and scepter.'
dismissed.note: The English already reads 'reigned over all, having disobedience as law and scepter', which is what the checker asks for.

dismissed.quote: Let them hear in response that if something is harmed, the occasion through which it is harmed is not therefore already base and evil.
dismissed.why: Source has 'not' (οὐκ) governing the whole conditional; English drops it, flipping the claim.
dismissed.note: The negation is present: the English says the occasion 'is not therefore already base and evil'.

dismissed.quote: having exchanged true life for death
dismissed.why: καταλλαξάμενος means 'having taken in exchange,' not active 'exchanging'; Adam received death in exchange for life.
dismissed.note: In English 'exchanged true life for death' means he gave up life and got death, which matches καταλλαξάμενος exactly.
